reviews.review:
Do not buy this game if you want a good story. Do not buy this game if you're into awesome graphics. Do not buy this game if you can't deal with a little permadeath. Do not buy this game if you want a game that hands you all the unlockables and characters on a silver platter. Do not buy this game... Well, you get the idea.

On the other hand, if you fit none of the above categories, you're golden. Risk of Rain is a Sci-Fi Roguelike which makes no excuses and no apologies. The story is minimal, the environments are decent if simple, and the gameplay is very, very unforgiving. And yes, you WILL die on your first run, I guarantee you. But soldier on, young gamer. Early runs are mostly dedicated to unlocking new characers (of which there are 12) and getting used to the game's mechanics. As the singular survivor (or survivors, if playing multiplayer) of a space shuttle crash, you must navigate a hostile alien planet in an effort to return to your spaceship, which has been commandeered by a mysterious alien named Providence. Beyond that, there's very little storytelling to be seen. Just survive to the end, gathering items and slaughtering your foes as you level up your character and try to make sense of what exactly is happening around you. As your character leaves the planet at the end of the final level, the camera pans over the level you've just finished, showing the piles of corpses of seemingly innocent creatures you just carved your way through to make it off the planet. You've survived- but at what cost?

Bittersweet ending aside, the game is a wild ride. Every one of the 12 characters is unique to play and powerful when mastered, from the agile and well-rounded Commando to the DOT-heavy, hit-and-run Acrid, to the bulky, slow-moving HAN-D. Enemies and bosses are varied, and each is unique in approach and danger level. While blasting your way through the armies of aliens is a fun time, don't take too long- the difficulty ramps up steadlily the longer your session goes on, and if you dawdle long enough, the RNG will happily toss legions of bosses and powered-up Elite enemies in place of the lowly mooks you've been fighting up to that point. Balancing steady progression and staying around long enough to grab all the helpful items and buffs is a constant struggle, even while you're trying to avoid getting torn to shreds by hostile wildlife. 

I've greatly enjoyed all of the time I've spent with Risk of Rain. And if you're willing to soldier on through death and brutal death, I'm sure you will too.

This really might be the most addicting game I have ever played. If you're on the fence about purchasing Risk Of Rain, let your $10 do the deciding and GET THIS GAME RIGHT NOW. 

Now, just a few things to note before you get started:

- You will die. A lot.
- No cheap tricks or power-leveling here -- this game requires /actual/ effort.
- This actually somehow makes it more enjoyable.
- The only thing more awesome than playing this game is playing this game with friends.
Amazing game with a huge amount of replay value and music to die for, which given its dificulty curve is most likley what you will do.
Thanks for the worst multiplayer support ever done on steam
